summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic abdominal pain due to suspected sphincter of Oddi dysfunction was readmitted due to worsening pain and nausea after a recent discharge. She underwent an ERCP with ampullary dilation, which showed no stones or blockages and improved bile flow. Post-procedure, she reported reduced pain, tolerated a diet advancement, and remained stable. She was discharged home the following day with no changes to her home medications except the addition of a stool softener and stimulant laxative. Follow-up with her GI specialist was planned for one week later.
